assumptions: E is a real inner-product space, not necessarily complete or finite dimensional. The function f:E→ℝ is globally G-Lipschitz, where G≥0.

A supplied vector g supports f at x globally: \[f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle\le f(y)\qquad\text{for every }y\in E.\] Existence of supporting vectors, convexity of f and differentiability are not additional premises.
mathematical_cores.boundary: This bounds each supplied global supporting vector. It constructs neither a subgradient nor a measurable/random oracle, gives no constrained-normal bound, and proves no optimization rate by itself. The existing sum_weighted_gap_le theorem consumes this estimate; Bench examples add no Registry credit.

open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.ConvexSubgradient
open scoped NNReal RealInnerProductSpace
variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]

example {f : E → ℝ} {G : ℝ≥0} {x g : E}
    (hf : LipschitzWith G f) (hs : SupportsAt f x g) : ‖g‖ ≤ (G : ℝ) := by
  have hs' := hs (x + g)
  change f x + inner ℝ g (x + g - x) ≤ f (x + g) at hs'
  rw [add_sub_cancel_left, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq] at hs'
  have hl : f (x + g) - f x ≤ (G : ℝ) * ‖g‖ := by
    calc
      f (x + g) - f x ≤ |f (x + g) - f x| := le_abs_self _
      _ ≤ (G : ℝ) * ‖g‖ := by
        simpa [Real.dist_eq, dist_eq_norm] using hf.dist_le_mul (x + g) x
  by_cases hg : ‖g‖ = 0
  · simp [hg]
  · have hp : 0 < ‖g‖ := lt_of_le_of_ne (norm_nonneg _) (Ne.symm hg)
    nlinarith

steps: Because the support relation is global, its test point may be y=x+g. Thus \[\|g\|^2=\langle g,g\rangle\le f(x+g)-f(x).\] This tests the supplied relation; it does not use a theorem constructing subgradients.
Global Lipschitz growth and the absolute-value bound give \[f(x+g)-f(x)\le|f(x+g)-f(x)|\le G\|g\|.\] Combining the inequalities yields \(\|g\|^2\le G\|g\|\).

If g=0 the conclusion is immediate from G≥0. Otherwise \(\|g\|>0\), so division by this strictly positive number gives \(\|g\|\le G\). No completeness, differentiability or finite-dimensional compactness is used.

For constrained support take E=ℝ, f≡0, G=0, C=[0,∞), x=0 and g=−1. Then \[f(0)+g(y-0)=-y\le0=f(y)\qquad(y\in C),\] but \(\|g\|=1>0=G\). The chosen point x+g=−1 is outside C. This refutes the constrained variant, not the globally quantified theorem.

assumptions: α and β are measurable spaces; β is nonempty and standard Borel. μ is any finite nonnegative measure on α×β, including the zero measure. No standard-Borel or nonempty assumption is imposed on α.

Let μ₁ be the first marginal and κ(a,db) a selected measurable regular conditional Markov kernel for the second coordinate given the first. You may use the existing finite-measure disintegration identity \[\mu(da,db)=\mu_1(da)\kappa(a,db).\] Its conditional characterization is only μ₁-almost everywhere; the selected version has mass one at every input.
The actual update retains a and resamples b: \[K((a,b),d(a',b'))=\delta_a(da')\kappa(a,db').\] Invariant means the measure equality μK=μ, not convergence from every starting measure.
mathematical_cores.boundary: This proves one actual conditional-resampling kernel preserves its finite joint target. It does not establish reversibility, irreducibility, uniqueness, convergence, a mixing rate, a generator-domain theorem or the Gibbs law of a continuous-time process. Conditional disintegration is allowed background, not reproved by this short task. The NL finite-state counterexample is not a separate Lean conclusion.

mathematical_cores.question: Prove μK=μ by identifying the measure after projecting to the retained coordinate and after applying the product kernel. Explain the role of measurability, the finite-measure disintegration, and the chosen conditional version on null fibers. Must μ be a probability measure? Give a finite-state example showing why this invariance result alone does not imply convergence from another initial probability law.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the measurable deterministic projection and its exact pushforward μ₁ under the actual input law.
Expresses the actual kernel as a deterministic composition and uses associativity and the measure–kernel product, not an independent product, to obtain μ₁⊗κ.
Applies the finite standard-Borel disintegration with the precise β hypotheses, permits zero μ and distinguishes global Markov normalization from almost-everywhere conditional support claims.
Gives the two-state retained-coordinate identity-kernel example, with a nonconverging initial law at TV distance 1/2, without mislabeling invariance as convergence or reversibility.

mathematical_cores.source_note: Original QA over the existing Samplinglib-owned HeatBath kernel and its finite-measure ConditionalResampling interface. Uses Mathlib's selected regular conditional distribution, kernel composition and Invariant definition. The discrete example specializes this general measurable-space result; this is not the earlier atomic-detailed-balance task or a new wrapper. No paper text, external dataset or restricted index is reproduced.
steps: The deterministic projection (a,b)↦a is measurable. Pushing μ through it gives exactly its first marginal \(\mu_1=(\mathrm{fst})_\#\mu\). This assertion uses the actual input μ, not an arbitrary starting law with a different first marginal.

The product kernel a↦δₐ⊗κ(a,·) is measurable because it is the product of the identity kernel and the measurable conditional kernel. Composition with the deterministic projection gives K. Associativity of kernel/measure composition yields \[\mu K=\mu_1(\mathrm{id}\times\kappa)=\mu_1\otimes\kappa.\] The last expression is a measure–kernel composition product, not the independent product of μ₁ and a fixed marginal.

The supplied finite-measure disintegration identity now gives \[\mu K=\mu_1\otimes\kappa=\mu.\] It is justified by the standard-Borel, nonempty β and finite μ interface. No density, positivity, normalization to mass one or division by a marginal density is required. For μ=0 both sides are zero; this is invariant as a finite measure, not a probability law.

Conditional versions agree in their prescribed conditional meaning only for μ₁-almost every a. Replacing them on a μ₁-null set does not change the integrated identity. The chosen global Markov version still yields a legitimate mass-one update there, but no claim about conditional support or convergence from such exceptional starting states follows.

For lack of convergence take α={0,1}, β={∗} with discrete measurable structures and \(\mu=(\tfrac12\delta_0+\tfrac12\delta_1)\otimes\delta_\ast\). The update never changes either coordinate, so K is the identity kernel. Starting from \(\rho=\delta_{(0,\ast)}\), \[\rho K^n=\rho,\qquad d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\rho K^n,\mu)=\tfrac12\quad(n\ge0).\] Thus the actual invariant target does not imply uniqueness, irreducibility, mixing or convergence from a different first marginal.
mathematical_cores.title: Why retaining one coordinate and conditionally resampling the other is invariant

case-1.assumptions: The only analytic hypotheses on f and g are the global Lipschitz bound LipschitzWith G f and the global supporting inequality SupportsAt f x g. Nonnegativity of G is built into its type. Neither convexity of f, differentiability, continuity of a derivative, existence of a minimizer, nor completeness of E is an additional assumption. The hypothesis concerns a support at the specified x, not an asserted support at every point.
case-1.conclusion: The norm of the given vector g is at most the same Lipschitz bound G, with G coerced from ℝ≥0 to ℝ: ‖g‖ ≤ (G : ℝ). This is a non-strict norm bound for each vector satisfying the stated global support hypothesis. It is not a claim of equality, uniqueness or existence of g, differentiability of f, or any bound on f(x) itself.
case-1.constants: G is an arbitrary finite nonnegative real bound, not assumed optimal or strictly positive; G = 0 is allowed. The conclusion has multiplicative constant exactly 1 and no additive error: ‖g‖ ≤ G after coercion. The supporting affine function has intercept f(x) and inner-product coefficient g, with no extra scale or tolerance. No dimension-dependent constant, sampling parameter or probability appears.
case-1.domains: E is an arbitrary type equipped with NormedAddCommGroup E and InnerProductSpace ℝ E, with their compatible real norm, metric and inner product. No completeness assumption is present. The function has type E → ℝ; x and g lie in E; G lies in ℝ≥0, the type of finite nonnegative real numbers. All Lipschitz and support comparisons range over the whole of E, not a feasible subset.
case-1.objects: A real-valued function f on a real inner-product space E, a nonnegative real Lipschitz bound G, a point x in E, and a vector g in E defining an affine global lower support y ↦ f(x) + ⟨g, y - x⟩. The claim bounds this given supporting vector; it does not assert that a supporting vector exists or identify g with a derivative.
case-1.quantifiers: Universally for every such E and its stated structures, every f : E → ℝ, every G : ℝ≥0, and every x,g : E: if f is LipschitzWith G and SupportsAt f x g, then ‖g‖ ≤ (G : ℝ). Expanded, the hypotheses say that for all u,v in E, |f(u) - f(v)| ≤ (G : ℝ) ‖u - v‖, and that for all y in E, f(x) + ⟨g, y - x⟩ ≤ f(y). No existential quantifier or restriction to almost-everywhere points occurs.
case-1.senses: SupportsAt is exactly an affine lower support over all y in E, using the real inner product ⟨g, y - x⟩; the displacement is y - x and the inequality faces toward f(y). LipschitzWith uses the metric distance, so the real-valued output distance is absolute difference and the input distance is the norm of a difference. The conclusion uses the vector norm on E. A merely local or constraint-set support would not be the stated hypothesis; a convex-analysis subgradient interpretation does not add convexity to the signature.

case-2.assumptions: The measure μ has μ(α × β) < ∞, allowing total mass zero and any finite total mass, not only one. The second-coordinate space β is nonempty and standard Borel, supplying a selected pointwise-normalized regular conditional Markov kernel for the second coordinate given the first. α has only a measurable-space assumption. No absolute continuity, density, product-factorization, coordinate independence, probability-measure hypothesis, irreducibility or ergodicity is assumed.
case-2.conclusion: The finite measure μ is invariant under the specified second-coordinate heat-bath update: μ.bind (heatBathSnd μ) = μ. Thus integrating one update against μ reproduces exactly μ, without changing its finite total mass or normalizing it. The conclusion does not state uniqueness of an invariant measure, convergence of iterates from other starting measures, a rate, reversibility or a detailed-balance identity. It also applies when μ is the zero measure.
case-2.constants: There is no numeric bound or free tuning constant. Finiteness is strict finiteness of μ's total mass, not a fixed positive value. The conditional Markov kernel has total mass exactly 1 at every a, and the construction therefore gives a Markov heat-bath kernel at every input, including when μ = 0. No division by μ's total mass or rescaling to a probability appears in the invariant-measure conclusion; μ may have mass 0, 1, or any other finite nonnegative value.
case-2.domains: α and β are arbitrary types with MeasurableSpace instances. β additionally has StandardBorelSpace β and Nonempty β; no standard-Borel, topological, nonempty or countability assumption is imposed on α. The product carries its product measurable space. μ : Measure (α × β) is an extended-nonnegative-real-valued measure with finite total mass. C : Kernel α β and K : Kernel (α × β) (α × β) are measurable measure-valued assignments.
case-2.objects: Measurable spaces α and β, a finite measure μ on α × β, the selected regular conditional kernel C = condDistrib Prod.snd Prod.fst μ from α to β, and the heat-bath kernel K = heatBathSnd μ on α × β. By definition K = (Kernel.id ×ₖ C) ∘ₖ Kernel.deterministic Prod.fst measurable_fst: from an input (a,b), it retains a and resamples the second coordinate with law C(a). Thus K((a,b), ·) = δ_a ⊗ C(a, ·), independently of the old b.
case-2.quantifiers: Universally for every α,β and the stated measurable-space, standard-Borel and nonempty structures, and every μ : Measure (α × β) with IsFiniteMeasure μ, the specifically defined heatBathSnd μ satisfies Kernel.Invariant K μ. Expanded, μ.bind K = μ as measures; equivalently, for every measurable S ⊆ α × β, ∫⁻ z, K(z,S) ∂μ = μ(S). The statement uses the chosen condDistrib construction; it does not explicitly quantify over all possible conditional-kernel versions.
case-2.senses: Kernel.Invariant is equality of measures after binding, not equality of the transition law at each input to μ. Composition first projects (a,b) to a and then applies the shared-input product of a Dirac identity kernel and C, so the first coordinate is preserved pointwise. The conditional/disintegration interpretation of C is characterized only almost everywhere for the first marginal of μ; its selected Markov normalization is pointwise, including inputs outside that almost-everywhere characterization. Invariance neither asserts a pointwise conditional formula at every a nor determines a unique version on marginal-null inputs.
